chapter: All chapters (Ch.1 hand-verified; Ch.2–40 parsed from The_First_City_Publication_Ready.pages)

characters.name: Narrator
characters.description: Adult male narrator; intelligent, restrained, dry, observant. Cinematic without sounding theatrical. He lets the unease come from the prose rather than announcing it.
characters.performance: Measured at the excavation; gradually cooler and tighter during descent; slower and more spacious inside the tomb; controlled shock after Kurash dies.

characters.name: Zik
characters.description: Experienced, dry, skeptical, technically precise. He notices details other people miss and rarely wastes words. Emotion is present but usually held under control.
characters.performance: Underplay jokes. Technical explanations should sound effortless, not lectured. Tighten noticeably around his father's compass and journal. Final 'that's new' is shock hidden behind dry control.

characters.name: Balag
characters.description: Large, grounded, dry-humored, cautious. Sounds like a man who trusts weight, stone and practical experience more than theories.
characters.performance: Low-key and economical. Humor lands because he does not perform it. His ward/religion exchange carries real unease under the joke. 'Kurash' is a genuine warning, not anger.

characters.name: Enhedu
characters.description: Quick, sharp, observant, amused by the men without becoming flippant. She is alert to material details and danger.
characters.performance: Keep teasing lines understated. As the group descends, humor narrows into focused attention. 'Then they chose the wrong door' should be confident, not cartoonishly fearless.

characters.name: Kurash
characters.description: Young, eager, curious, hungry for a better life, not stupid. He asks too many questions because he wants to learn and wants what the expedition might buy him.
characters.performance: Faster than the others, but natural. Excitement increases around the treasure. His last choices should sound like rationalization and temptation, not villainy.

characters.name: Bel-iddin
characters.role: Zik's father; remembered teacher and journal voice
characters.description: Older, precise, intimate, grave. A teacher who expects Zik to think. His remembered advice is calm certainty; the journal carries more urgency.
characters.performance: Memory lines are dry and instructional. First two journal lines are intimate and grave. The final second-door warning is the same man under strain: urgent, pressed, but still intelligible.

characters.name: Dead King
characters.role: Crowned skeleton in the sealed tomb
characters.description: Ancient, dry, unnervingly calm. This voice is reference-conditioned by Chatterbox Nano from a real gravelly whispered performance rather than manufactured with post-processing noise.
characters.performance: Nearly whispered, brittle and scratchy from the actual reference performance. Threatening because it is quiet and certain. 'Zikir Ashur.' should sound like damaged vocal cords forcing out a name. Leave a long beat after it.

characters.name: Ninsun
characters.description: Former university scholar working the lower archives. Precise, formal, few contractions, dry academic humor. Her sister vanished into a shifted district.
characters.performance: Level and controlled; under fear she becomes MORE exact, not louder. Contrast with Enhedu: archive vs street.

characters.name: The Collector
characters.description: Narrow man, narrow face, narrow beard. Smooth, patient, faintly amused; answers a different question than the one asked.
characters.performance: Never raises his voice. Close-miked even when 'outside the shutter' — he sounds nearer than he is.

characters.name: Mardu
characters.description: Old custodian, 31 years at the door. White hair, dark brows. Voice old, not weak, worn smooth by repetition.
characters.performance: Bone-dry bureaucratic wit delivered straight. Quietly kind underneath.

characters.name: Zik's Mother
characters.description: Frail, coughing, sharp-eyed. Lives above a potter's kiln. Sees straight through her son.
characters.performance: Soft, plain, unsentimental. Tired breath.

characters.name: Old Scribe
characters.description: Gray-bearded teacher with a reed cane. Knew Bel-iddin.
characters.performance: Wry and a little cantankerous. NOTE: his imitation of Bel-iddin is assigned to Bel-iddin's voice.

characters.name: Apprentice Boy
characters.description: Clay-stained fingertips, fell asleep on a tablet.
characters.performance: Shy, respectful.

characters.name: Messenger Boy
characters.description: All elbows and caution.
characters.performance: Cagey, frustrated by questions, then eager for the coin.

characters.name: False Scribe
characters.description: Well-dressed young scribe carrying a 'message from the Collector' — the Collector later says he never sent him.
characters.performance: Nervous until the end of the alley; final lines drop into a slower, older register (see line notes).

characters.name: Water-Seller
characters.description: Bickering over measures.
characters.performance: Comic, indignant.

characters.name: Water Customer
characters.description: Accuses the seller of thumbing the cup.
characters.performance: Comic, deadpan.

characters.name: Archive Guard
characters.description: Bored guard, increasingly suspicious.
characters.performance: Gruff; muffled through the door when calling down.

characters.name: Inn Cook
characters.description: Ladle raised like a weapon.
characters.performance: Harried, loud.

characters.name: The Man Who Refused
characters.description: Gaunt, gray skin, cloudy eyes, dust-fused linen. Voice sounds unused.
characters.performance: Slow, hoarse, weary calm with bleak dry humor.

characters.name: The Remainder
characters.description: Zik as the City left him: worn, not old. 'It sounded exactly like him.'
characters.performance: Use Zik's base voice, exhausted and roughened. Never a different actor.

characters.name: The Statue
characters.description: One line: 'You are late.'
characters.performance: Dry, flat, utterly unimpressed — a clerk ticking a name off a very long list.

characters.name: The City
characters.role: The City's own voice (basin, echoes, words in the mind)
characters.description: Not fully human. When the City imitates a person, those lines are assigned to that person with a CITY MIMIC note instead.
characters.performance: Whispered, wet, close. Heavy processing allowed here only.
